title: Paint the middle nail on a silicone practice hand
instruction: Paint the middle fingernail on the silicone practice hand red. Keep the silicone around that nail clean.
context: Applying a clean coat is a core manicure service. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 152,770 manicurist and pedicurist jobs in May 2025. A fixed silicone hand isolates brush control along the middle fingernail boundary.
setup: A fixed five-finger silicone practice hand rests on a dark gray 163 × 113 × 6 mm pad. Its wrist extends in +x, and its fingers point towards −x. The curved 17 × 12 mm middle nail is centred at (235, 0) mm on the centreline between the arm bases. A 23 g red applicator with a 27 × 24 × 38 mm handle and 5.6 mm effective tip starts upright at (163, 175) mm.
scoring: A held upright applicator transfers red when its modelled tip is within 1.5 mm of the nail plane while making continuous strokes. Full score requires ≥85% nail coverage and spill on the surrounding skin ≤2% of nail area for 0.3 s. Otherwise score the final nail coverage fraction × max(0, 1 − 4 × spill fraction), capped at 0.99.
reset_notes: Reset restores the fixed starting pose, returns the applicator upright and clears deposited polish.
fidelity: Procedural five-finger silicone hand with curved nail shells, box colliders, and a planar 0.75 mm paint coverage grid around the middle nail. The preloaded compliant foam tip is an analytical 4 mm extension. The model omits bristle flex, drying, pressure-dependent flow and skin deformation.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 after reaching the 2,400-step limit without errors. Scripted joint-target replay: 1.0 in 448 steps, with 85.40% nail coverage and spill equal to 1.10% of nail area.
